Petition of Rural Telephone Company for a waiver )
from the requirement to file a new request for money)
from the Nevada Universal Service Fund. ) Docket No. 26-05003

PRESENT: Chair Hayley Williamson
Commissioner Tammy Cordova

Assistant Commission Secretary Trisha Osborne
ORDER
The Public Utilities Commission of Nevada (“Commission”) makes the following
findings of fact and conclusions of law:
I. INTRODUCTION
On May 4, 2026, Rural Telephone Company (“Rural Telephone”) filed with the Public
Utilities Commission of Nevada (“Commission”) a petition, designated as Docket No. 26-05003,
requesting a waiver from the requirement to file a new request for money from the Nevada
Universal Service Fund (“NUSF’”).
I. SUMMARY
The Commission grants the petition.
Til. PROCEDURAL HISTORY
* On May 4, 2026, Rural Telephone filed the petition pursuant to the Nevada Revised Statutes
(“NRS”) and the Nevada Administrative Code (“NAC”) Chapters 703 and 704, including, but
not limited to, NAC 704.680482 and NAC 703.540.
* On May 11, 2026, the Commission issued a Notice of Petition for Affirmative Relief.

* The Regulatory Operations Staff of the Commission (“Staff”) participates as a matter of right
pursuant to NRS 703.301.

* On June 3, 2026, Staff filed comments recommending approval of Rural Telephone’s petition.

Docket No. 26-05003 Page 2

* On June 25, 2026, the Commission’s Office of General Counsel (“General Counsel”) filed a
briefing memorandum recommending the Commission grant Rural Telephone’s petition.

* On June 30, 2026, at a regularly scheduled agenda meeting, the Commission voted to adopt the
recommendations contained in General Counsel’s briefing memorandum.

IV. PETITION
Rural Telephone’s Position

1. Rural Telephone requests waiver from the requirement to file a new request for
money from the NUSF. (Pet. at 1.). Specifically, Rural Telephone seeks approval of a two-year
waiver to file a new request pursuant to NAC 704.68048 to establish its annual draw from the
NUSF while continuing to receive its annual NUSF draw of $268,484 for two years until 2029.
(d.)

2. Rural Telephone explains that its last rate case (Docket No. 21-06047), which was
resolved through a stipulation with Staff, resulted in Rural Telephone’s current level of funding
through 2026; however, absent the requested relief, it would be required to file a rate case in
2026 to determine NUSF support for 2027. (/d. at 4-5.)

3. Rural Telephone provides that pursuant to NAC 704.68048(2)(c), as a small-scale
provider of last resort that draws from the NUSF, Rural Telephone must file a new request for
money every five years in a general rate case. (/d. at 4.) However, NAC 704.680482 provides
that Rural Telephone may petition for waiver of not more than two years from the rate case filing
requirement provided it satisfies NAC 704.680482(3) and the Commission finds that, based upon
information detailed in NAC 704.680282(4), it is not collecting excess earnings. (/d.)

4. Rural Telephone submits that it provided the information required by NAC

704.680482(4), including a) its annual operating revenue, expenses, and rate base as of its most

Docket No. 26-05003 Page 3

recent annual report;! b) Rural Telephone did not make any specific adjustments in its last rate
case given that it was a “black box” stipulation; c) Rural Telephone’s Commission-approved
return on rate base is 9.25 percent using a return on equity of 10.18 percent”; and d) it received
federal universal support totaling $453,894 in 2024. (/d. at 6-7.)

5. Rural Telephone states that it utilized consultants to update its annual report to
reflect the final cost study that was submitted to the National Exchange Carrier Association,
which also captured final updates in Rural Telephone’s 2024 audited financial statements,
including provisions for taxes. (/d. at 7-8.) Rural Telephone provides that the updated numbers
demonstrate that Rural Telephone’s rate of return was 3.77 percent, with a return on common
equity of 3.68 percent, falling below the Commission-approved 9.25 percent rate of return using
areturn of equity of 10.18 percent approved in Docket No. 21-05047. (/d. at 8.)

6. Rural Telephone states that its senior accounting employee recently retired and
other changes have been made in senior management. (/d.) Rural Telephone explains that it
would be a financial and operational burden to file a rate case in 2026 or 2027 while adjusting to
its new personnel changes. (/d.) Moreover, Rural Telephone is not collecting excess earnings.
(d.). Given those circumstances, Rural Telephone provides that it would be in the public
interest to grant its petition. (/d.)

Staff's Position
7. Staff recommends that the Commission approve Rural Telephone’s request for a

two-year waiver. (Staff’s Comments at 4.) Staff states that Rural Telephone provided the

information required by NAC 704.880482(4) and agrees with the company that granting its
waiver would be in the public interest. (/d. at 3.)

8. Staff explains that the petition is in the public interest because the Commission,
including Staff and Rural Telephone, are currently engaged in an investigation and rulemaking
that may make the significant use of public resources required for a general rate case, and the
financial and operational burden of such a proceeding, unnecessary by the time Rural Telephone
is required to make a new NUSF request. (/d.) Moreover, Staff notes that Rural Telephone’s
petition relies on the underlying stipulation in Docket No. 21-06047 where the parties did not
agree on an Alternative America Cost Model allocation methodology and the construction of
NAC 704.680482(4)(d), issues which may be more efficiently resolved in the ongoing
investigation and rulemaking before parties are required to address them in a general rate case.
(Id. at 3-4.)

Commission Discussion and Findings

9. NAC 704.680482(1) provides a vehicle for telecommunications companies who
are small-scale providers of last resort to seek a two-year waiver of the filing of a general rate
case. NAC 704.680482(2) gives the Commission discretion to grant a limited, two-year waiver
to small scale providers of last resort provided that the company seeking waiver demonstrates
that granting of the waiver is 1) in the public interest; and 2;) upon examining the information
required by NAC 704.680482(4), the Commission determines that the company is not over-
earning. Here, Rural Telephone met the technical requirements of NAC 704.680482 and
demonstrated that such a waiver is in the public interest.

10. Specifically, the Commission finds that in Rural Telephone’s petition, it provided:

its most recent annual operating revenue, annual operating expenses and rate base as a small-

Docket No. 26-05003 Page 5

scale provider of last resort, based upon its most recent annual report at the time of filing;
detailed adjustments, or the lack thereof, made in its last general rate case; its current
Commission-approved return on equity and a calculation of what the company is actually
earning; and disclosed the total amount of federal universal support that Rural Telephone
received in 2024 in satisfaction of NAC 704.680482(4). Rural Telephone also provided updated
calculations of its return on equity made after the filing of its annual report to reflect the final
cost study that was submitted to the National Exchange Carrier Association.

11. The Commission finds that Rural Telephone’s most recent annual report filed
with the Commission, and an updated annual report provided with its petition, demonstrate that
Rural Telephone is earning a return on equity below their authorized level. Notably, Rural
Telephone’s current authorized rate of return is 9.25 percent. Based upon the figures contained
in its 2024 annual report, Rural Telephone operated with a rate of return of -7.10 percent. An
examination of updated numbers contained in a supplemental update produced by third-party
consultants placed that figure at 3.68 percent. However, even with updated numbers, Rural
Telephone is not exceeding its authorized rate of return, thus satisfying NAC 704.680482(3)(b).

12. The Commission finds and agrees with Rural Telephone and Staff that approval
of the instant petition would be in the public interest. More specifically, given Rural
Telephone’s transitional period with senior accounting employees, its lower earnings relative to
its authorized rate of return, and the pending investigation and rulemaking in Docket No. 24-
12030 that might reduce expenditures and burdens involved with rate case proceedings, a two-
year waiver would serve the public interest. Accordingly, the Commission grants the petition.

Therefore, it is ordered:
